lessons.culture: In Gulf malls the assistants often come from South Asia or elsewhere and may answer in English, so greeting with السلام عليكم and using the borrowed sizes لارج, ميديم and سمول gets you served fastest. Trying something on and saying it does not fit is normal and never rude.

exercises.prompt: A shop assistant asks you: "شو مقاسك؟" Answer that your size is large.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: The borrowed English sizes لارج, ميديم and سمول are what people really say in shops.

exercises.prompt: The assistant asks a woman: "شو مقاسچ؟" Answer that your size is small.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but stiff; in a shop the borrowed size word is what is said.

exercises.tip: مقاسچ, with the ch sound, is how the Gulf addresses a woman; a man is مقاسك.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "أبي _____ لو سمحت." English meaning: I want a shirt, please.

too_formal.feedback: A roundabout formal way to describe a shirt; the everyday word is قميص.

exercises.tip: أبي plus the item is the everyday way to ask for something in the UAE and Kuwait.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "هذا وايد _____ علي." English meaning: This is too big for me.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatical but bookish; people just say كبير with وايد.

exercises.tip: وايد means very, much or a lot, and is one of the most Gulf words there is.

exercises.prompt: Say in Gulf Arabic: "Can I try it on?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: أقدر, "I can", opens a polite request; the ق is said g in the Gulf.

exercises.prompt: Say in Gulf Arabic: "Where's the fitting room?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: وين is the everyday word for where; أين belongs to books and news.

exercises.prompt: Which word means "too tight"?

too_formal.feedback: Fine in writing, but in speech وايد replaces جداً.

exercises.tip: The opposite is واسع (loose, wide). Some Gulf speakers say ضيّج with a j.

exercises.prompt: How do you ask a man "What's your size?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: -ك is for a man; for a woman the Gulf ending is -چ.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to say: "This is too big for me."

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; جداً is replaced by وايد.

exercises.tip: Both وايد كبير and كبير وايد are natural.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to say: "Do you have a bigger size?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: عندكم, "you all have", is the polite way to ask a shop.

response.english: The blue one looks nicer on you.

lessons.culture: Assistants in the Gulf enjoy helping you choose and will often bring out several options; saying a color does not suit you is heard as useful, not rude. Color words follow the Gulf sound of ق as g, so blue is أزرق, said azrag.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "شرايك في هالفستان؟" Say it is very nice.

too_formal.feedback: Correct and polite, but not how friends talk in a shop.

exercises.tip: حلو is the everyday word for nice, pretty or good-looking.

exercises.prompt: The shopkeeper asks: "أي واحد تنصحني؟" Recommend the black one.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatical but bookish; in a shop it is just أنصحك بالأسود.

exercises.tip: Use أنصحك to a man and أنصحچ to a woman.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "يعجبني اللون _____." English meaning: I like the blue color.

too_formal.feedback: A literary word for azure; the everyday word is الأزرق.

exercises.tip: In the Gulf ق is said g, so أزرق is azrag.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "هذا _____ وايد علي." English meaning: This is too dark for me.

too_formal.feedback: A correct word for dark, but in a shop غامق is what is said.

exercises.tip: The opposite is فاتح, light.

exercises.prompt: Say in Gulf Arabic: "Do you have another color?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: ثاني means second and also other; هذا ثاني is another one.

exercises.prompt: Say in Gulf Arabic: "I haven't decided yet."

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; for yet, the Gulf says للحين with ما plus the verb.

exercises.tip: للحين means still or yet, and الحين means now.

exercises.prompt: Which word means "light" (a light color)?

too_formal.feedback: Means bright or shining, not light as opposed to dark.

exercises.tip: Say لون فاتح for a light color and لون غامق for a dark one.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "Just give me this one"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; in speech it is عطني and بس.

exercises.tip: عطني is said to a man; to a woman it is عطيني.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to say: "This color doesn't suit me."

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA with لا; in speech the negative is ما.

exercises.tip: ما goes right before the verb.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to say: "Which is nicer, red or blue?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA with أم; in the Gulf it is لو, or.

exercises.tip: لو between two options means or.

lessons.culture: In the Gulf, bargaining is expected in a souq, at a gold or textile stall or over something large, but prices in malls and brand shops are fixed. A friendly عشانك, "for your sake", is the shopkeeper's usual way of dropping the price.

exercises.prompt: You ask "بكم هذا؟" and the shopkeeper says "بمية وخمسين". Say it is very expensive.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but far too formal for a shop counter.

exercises.tip: غالي is expensive and رخيص is cheap.

exercises.prompt: You and the shopkeeper agree on a price. Say "Ok, we agreed."

too_formal.feedback: Sounds like a contract; people just say خلاص، اتفقنا.

exercises.tip: خلاص, "done, that's it", closes any deal in the Gulf.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "_____ هذا؟" English meaning: How much is this?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but ثمن is a written word; in a shop it is بكم.

exercises.tip: You may also hear شكثر in Kuwait for how much.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "هذا _____ سعر." English meaning: This is the final price.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; in a souq you say آخر سعر, last price.

exercises.tip: آخر means last, and آخر سعر is how a shopkeeper ends the haggling.

exercises.prompt: Say in Gulf Arabic: "Can you lower the price?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: In the Gulf ق is said g, so تقدر is tigdar.

exercises.prompt: Say in Gulf Arabic: "Isn't there cheaper than this?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: أرخص is cheaper, the comparative of رخيص.

exercises.prompt: Which word means "expensive"?

too_formal.feedback: A correct word for costly, but written rather than spoken.

exercises.tip: The opposite is رخيص.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "Lower it a bit for me"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; in a souq it is نزّل لي شوي.

exercises.tip: شوي, a little, softens a request and is heard everywhere in the Gulf.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to say: "I want a discount because I'm buying a lot."

response.english: Is everything ok, what's the problem?

lessons.culture: Many Gulf shops prefer an exchange or store credit to a cash refund, and the receipt makes the conversation short. A genuine defect is normally accepted without argument, and ما قصّرت, "you did not fall short", is the usual warm thanks for good service.

exercises.prompt: The assistant asks: "خير، شو المشكلة؟" Say there is a defect.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: فيه, "in it there is", is the usual Gulf way to say there is.

exercises.prompt: You asked if they give money back and the assistant says they only exchange. Say "Fine, can I exchange it for a bigger size?"

too_formal.item: حسناً، هل يمكنني استبداله بمقاس أكبر؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; in the Gulf it is زين for fine and أقدر for can I.

exercises.tip: زين means good or fine and is the Gulf word for ok.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "عندي _____." English meaning: I have the receipt.

too_formal.feedback: A correct formal term; in shops it is الفاتورة.

exercises.tip: الفاتورة is the bill, invoice or receipt.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "هذا مقاس _____." English meaning: This is the wrong size.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; people say غلط for wrong.

exercises.tip: غلط works for anything wrong: a size, a color or an order.

exercises.prompt: Say in Gulf Arabic: "I want to return this shirt."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, but it is not what people say in a shop in the Gulf.

exercises.tip: هالـ is a spoken short form of هذا ال.

exercises.prompt: Say in Gulf Arabic: "When did you buy it?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; simply متى اشتريته is enough.

exercises.tip: To a woman the verb ends with ي: اشتريتيه.

exercises.prompt: Which word means "a defect"?

too_formal.feedback: A correct word, but for clothes people say عيب.

exercises.tip: عيب also means shame, so context decides.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "I don't have the receipt"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; in speech it is ما عندي.

exercises.tip: ما عندي is the everyday way to say I don't have.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to say: "This isn't what I ordered."

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; the Gulf uses مب (UAE) or مو (Kuwait) and اللي.

exercises.tip: مب is common in the UAE and مو in Kuwait; both mean not.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to say: "I want to exchange it for another one."

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; in a shop it is أبي أبدّله بثاني.

exercises.tip: بثاني, with another, uses ثاني for other.

challenge.title: A Shopping Trip in the Souq
challenge.instructions: Write and act a shopping conversation of at least 10 lines. It must include asking for an item by size, discussing a color, checking the price, bargaining at least once, and a return or exchange with the receipt mentioned. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 6 and include both a masculine and a feminine form of address.
required_elements: An opening request using أبي and a clothing item.
A size question using شو مقاسك؟ or شو مقاسچ؟
At least one bargaining line using تقدر تنزّل السعر؟ or نزّل لي شوي.
A final price line using آخر سعر.
A return or exchange line using أرجّع or أبدّل.
A mention of the receipt using الفاتورة.
A closing thank-you such as مشكور، ما قصّرت or الله يعطيك العافية.
